description: 2 tactical challenges for Black in the Elephant Trap. Play 4...Nbd7! and punish the greedy 6.Nxd5??.

drills.briefExplanation: 4...Nbd7! 5.cxd5 exd5 6.Nxd5?? Nxd5 — the 'free' knight costs White a piece.
drills.description: Black to play. White pins with 4.Bg5 — set the Elephant Trap with 4...Nbd7!.
drills.explanation: The Elephant Trap: 4...Nbd7 looks passive, but it sets a deadly trap. After 5.cxd5 exd5, the natural-looking 6.Nxd5?? grabs what seems to be a free pawn — and 6...Nxd5 simply takes the knight, which has no defender. Note the fancy 7.Bxd8?? doesn't even work: the f6 knight covers d8. White just drops a piece; the 'trap' is that the pawn was never really free.
drills.name: The Elephant Steps In

drills.briefExplanation: 5...exd5 6.Bxf6 Nxf6 7.e3 Be7 — recapture toward the center and complete development.
drills.description: Black to play. White took on d5 — recapture correctly and avoid any tricks.
drills.explanation: When White doesn't cooperate with 6.Nxd5??, Black just plays solidly: 5...exd5 opens the e-file for later use, and after 6.Bxf6 Nxf6 7.e3 Be7 Black has a sound Queen's Gambit Declined structure with easy development. The trap stays set for next time — and Black is never worse for having played the useful 4...Nbd7.
drills.name: The Solid Recapture
